text: The hiring process begins when a department submits an approved role request. The request should include the job title, responsibilities, required skills, and reporting manager.
The HR team publishes the vacancy on approved channels and collects applications. Applicants are shortlisted against the role requirements and relevant experience.
Shortlisted candidates are invited to complete the required assessments or technical screening. Assessment criteria should be consistent for candidates applying to the same role.
Candidates who pass screening attend interview rounds with the hiring team. Interviewers submit their feedback promptly using the standard evaluation format.
HR coordinates reference checks, approvals, and the final offer. The selected candidate receives joining instructions after accepting the offer.
Employees should keep their personal and contact information updated with the HR team. Changes to bank details, address, or emergency contacts should be reported through the approved process.
The organization maintains employee records for employment administration and statutory requirements. Access to these records is limited to authorized personnel.
Employees should follow the organization’s code of conduct and workplace communication guidelines. Concerns about workplace behaviour may be raised with HR or the designated reporting contact.
New employees complete onboarding activities, including document submission and an introduction to company policies. Managers should clarify role expectations and initial priorities.
Employment letters, experience letters, and other HR documents can be requested through the HR helpdesk. Requests are processed after identity and record details are verified.
Employees should submit planned leave requests through the approved leave management system. Requests should be made in advance so managers can plan team coverage.
Leave approval depends on the available balance, team requirements, and the applicable leave category. Employees should wait for confirmation before treating planned leave as approved.
For unexpected illness or emergencies, employees should inform their manager as soon as reasonably possible. Supporting documents may be requested where required by policy.
Public holidays and weekly offs are handled according to the organization’s published holiday calendar. Any work scheduled on these days should be agreed with the manager in advance.
Leave balances and request status can be checked in the leave management system. Questions about eligibility, corrections, or special cases should be directed to HR.

Employees should inform their manager if a medical issue affects their ability to work or attend the workplace. Personal medical information should be shared only with authorized personnel when necessary.
Medical leave requests must follow the organization’s leave application process. A medical certificate may be required depending on the duration and applicable rules.
Employees who need workplace adjustments should contact HR to discuss suitable arrangements. Requests are reviewed with due regard for privacy and operational requirements.
In a workplace emergency, contact the designated emergency response team or local emergency services. Do not delay urgent medical attention while completing administrative formalities.
Any available health insurance or reimbursement benefit is subject to the applicable plan terms. Employees should consult HR or the insurer for coverage, claim documents, and deadlines.
A Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is used to understand why an incident or failure occurred. The objective is to identify contributing causes and prevent recurrence rather than assign blame.
The incident owner should record the date, impact, affected systems or teams, and a clear description of the event. Relevant logs, reports, and supporting evidence should be preserved.
The team reviews the sequence of events and identifies immediate triggers as well as underlying process or system weaknesses. Conclusions should be supported by evidence.
Corrective actions address the current issue, while preventive actions reduce the chance of similar incidents. Each action should have an owner and a target completion date.
The RCA is reviewed by the relevant stakeholders and stored in the approved knowledge repository. Action owners should provide updates until all agreed actions are closed.
All technical changes should be tracked in the approved version-control system. Developers should use descriptive branch names and commit messages that explain the purpose of each change.
Code changes should follow the project’s style, architecture, and security guidelines. Secrets, credentials, and private keys must never be committed to source control.
Before a change is merged, it should pass the required tests and review checks. Reviewers should examine correctness, maintainability, performance, and potential security risks.
Deployments should follow the documented release process and use the approved environments. Changes with significant user impact should include a rollback or recovery plan.
Technical incidents and important system decisions should be documented for future reference. The relevant owner should keep setup instructions, dependencies, and troubleshooting notes current.
Business travel should be approved by the employee’s manager before bookings are made. The request should state the purpose, destination, dates, and expected expenses.
Employees should use approved booking channels and choose reasonable travel options. Any exception to the travel guidelines should receive prior authorization where possible.
Receipts and invoices should be collected for eligible travel expenses. Claims should include the business purpose, date, amount, and required supporting documents.
Expense claims must be submitted through the approved reimbursement process within the stated submission period. Personal expenses and unsupported claims may be excluded.
The manager and finance team review claims against the applicable policy and available approvals. Reimbursements are processed after the claim is verified and approved.
